text:
The tenant's adverse possession most likely began one month after the widow's death in 1986, when the tenant decided to stay and stopped paying rent, so the 20-year period would have expired around 2006, before the Boy Scouts discovered their claim in 2009. The team note is wrong: a landlord's death does not extinguish a lease, because the estate or devisee takes subject to it, so the tenant's possession stayed permissive until it clearly repudiated the owner's title. Whether stopping rent and staying counts as a clear repudiation, especially without notice to the owner, depends on the jurisdiction, and if it does not, the clock may have started later and the Scouts' claim could still be timely.

CONFIDENCE: 50
